Class RootResource

java.lang.Object
ca.refundr.highspring.api.resource.AbstractResource
ca.refundr.highspring.api.resource.RootResource
public final class RootResource extends AbstractResource
Root of the HTTP resource tree — the first object RequestFilter creates for each call.

Why this class exists

Think of URLs as a folder tree. RootResource is the “/” folder. It does not implement shopping features itself; it either:

  • Answers GET / with a tiny JSON hello message, or
  • Hands longer paths to Version1Resource under /v1/.

How routing starts

RequestFilter does roughly: 

   String path = "v1/cart/";          // from the request URI, no leading slash
   RootResource root = new RootResource(requestScope);
   AbstractResource match = root.getByPath(path);
   match.processRequest();            // calls httpGet / httpPost / …

AbstractResource.getByPath(String) (inherited) checks this node’s getRelativePath(), then asks getDescendantByPath(String) for children. Here the only child is Version1Resource.

Adding a new API version later

You would add another child next to Version1Resource, e.g. Version2Resource with getRelativePath() = "v2/". Old clients keep calling /v1/....
